topic.title: The iPhone that's never in stock
topic.claim: The iPhone 17 base model going out of stock right through Diwali while the Pro and Pro Max sit on shelves isn't bad planning, it's an upsell.
topic.behaviour: Croma, Vijay Sales and dealers in Nehru Place report zero iPhone 17 base inventory, turning away 10-12 customers a day, while buyers get pushed toward costlier Pro/Pro Max units on Amazon and Flipkart.
topic.mechanism: Initial Pro batches were imported and ready to sell while cheaper Made-in-India units are still ramping up, so the stock gap happens to sit exactly where it benefits the higher-margin model.
topic.group: upper middle class festive-season gadget buyers
real_details: Croma and Vijay Sales report zero iPhone 17 inventory
initial iPhone 17 Pro batches were imported while Made-in-India Pro units are still ramping up
topic.news_peg: iPhone 17 stockouts across Indian retail during Diwali 2026 shopping season
topic.why_now: peak festive buying is happening right now and the base model still isn't back

sources.fact: Croma and Vijay Sales are facing a severe iPhone 17 stock shortage this Diwali season, turning away about a dozen customers a day while Amazon and Flipkart get prioritized for the pricier Pro and Pro Max models.
sources.excerpt: iPhone 17 supply crunch leaves retailers empty-handed this Diwali — India's large retail chains, including Croma and Vijay Sales, are experiencing a severe shortage of iPhone 17 units during the crucial pre-Diwali shopping season, with many outlets completely out of stock and unable to commit timelines for incoming inventory. Retailers say the root of the problem is Apple's continued dependence on imports for the iPhone 17 Pro models, which has led to very limited allocations to third-party offline and online retail channels this year. As a result, retail staff are reportedly turning away up to a dozen customers per day, calling it a significant missed opportunity during the peak sales period. The uneven distribution strategy has led to further frustration, with some smaller dealers and chains complaining that company-owned stores and e-commerce platforms—Amazon and Flipkart are stocking the higher-end iPhone 17 Pro and Max models—are prioritized for fresh stock.

sources.fact: Croma, Vijay Sales and dealers at Delhi's Nehru Place have run out of iPhone 17 stock, with a retail chain manager confirming inventory is stuck on Apple's distribution side amid Diwali demand.
sources.excerpt: iPhone 17 shortage hits Indian retailers amid Diwali season frenzy — Retail giants such as Croma and Vijay Sales, along with local dealers at Delhi's Nehru Place, Asia's largest electronics market, are running out of iPhone 17 stock amid soaring demand. Retailers say they are turning away 10–12 customers daily due to the shortage, calling it a missed sales opportunity during the festival season. According to a retail chain manager: "We have no iPhone 17 inventory currently and no visibility on when new stock will arrive. It's stuck from the company's distribution side." Apple's uneven distribution has reportedly diverted customers to company-owned Apple stores and e-commerce platforms, such as Amazon and Flipkart, which are mainly selling high-end variants like the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max, starting at ₹1,54,900.

sources.fact: While the base iPhone 17 is scarce, iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max units are actively being discounted and sold on Croma, Amazon and Flipkart during the festive season.
sources.excerpt: Both models are offered at a discount during Croma's Festival of Dreams sale until 31 October, with availability subject to stock. The Croma offer shows the iPhone 17 Pro 256GB priced at Rs.1,30,490, compared to its MRP of Rs.1,34,900. The iPhone 17 Pro Max 256GB is priced at Rs.1,43,990 at Croma, compared with its MRP of Rs.1,49,900. Flipkart lists the lowest configuration of the device at Rs.1,34,900. Flipkart users who hold an Axis Bank credit card can avail a discount of Rs.4,500.

topic.title: Campa's ₹10 bottle and Coke's refusal to match it
topic.claim: Coca-Cola publicly refusing to match Campa's ₹10 price is more telling than Campa's price itself.
topic.behaviour: Campa sells a 200ml bottle at ₹10 and 500ml at ₹20, roughly half of Coke and Pepsi, crossing ₹4,700 crore in FY26 gross sales, while Coca-Cola's CEO rejected 'irrational pricing' and PepsiCo responded with a ₹5,700 crore India manufacturing push instead of discounting.
topic.mechanism: Global cola brands protect their price band even at the cost of share because the price itself is part of what they're selling, admitting a ₹10 bottle can compete would undercut the premium story the whole brand runs on.
topic.group: regular soft drink buyers, kirana shoppers
real_details: Coca-Cola CEO Henrique Braun rejected 'irrational pricing'
PepsiCo countered with a ₹5,700 crore India manufacturing push
topic.news_peg: Campa vs Coca-Cola price war during the 2026 festive season
topic.why_now: visible on kirana shelves and fridges right through this festive season

sources.fact: Coca-Cola's leadership said it will not chase 'irrational' pricing moves by rivals like Campa Cola, even if it means short-term share loss in India's festive-season price war.
sources.excerpt: On Not Chasing Aggressive Pricing: "You might lose share in one quarter here, or you got something else and another player will have an irrational play on pricing" On Strategic Response: "It is how you don't overreact to noise, but really act on the signals" The Coca-Cola Company's leadership stated the beverage firm would not overreact to aggressive pricing by competitors in India, despite Reliance Industries' Campa Cola emerging as a serious challenger. The company views short-term market share fluctuations as normal in developing markets and says this won't alter their long-term strategy. Campa Cola has become India's fourth-largest carbonated soft drink brand in FY26 with sales exceeding ₹4,700 crore, targeting impulse purchases through competitive price points like ₹10 and ₹20 bottles. Newer entrants collectively captured 6-7% market share by FY26, up from 2% in FY24, according to Crisil Ratings.

sources.fact: Campa crossed Rs 4,700 crore in FY26 gross sales and gained double-digit market share in key markets, as announced by Isha Ambani at Reliance's AGM.
sources.excerpt: Campa achieved gross sales exceeding Rs 4,700 crore ($496 million) in FY26, securing double-digit market share in several key markets, according to statements made at Reliance Industries' 49th Annual General Meeting. Isha Ambani declared: "Campa has emerged as a strong challenger in the carbonated soft drinks category, achieving over Rs 4,700 crore in gross sales during FY26 and gaining double-digit market share in important markets." She added a tagline: "Campa is not merely a brand. It is India ka Thanda." The beverage brand's expansion helped drive RCPL's overall beverage business growth to 3.2 times year-on-year in FY26. Reliance acquired Campa Cola from Pure Drinks Group in 2022 for approximately Rs 22 crore and has since aggressively expanded distribution nationwide.

sources.fact: PepsiCo's CEO confirmed a committed ₹5,700 crore investment in India manufacturing capacity through 2030 rather than responding to Campa's pricing with discounts.
sources.excerpt: PepsiCo's CEO stated: "from 2025 to 2030, we have committed almost ₹5,700 crore of investments." The funding targets manufacturing expansion across three states. The company is establishing facilities in Madhya Pradesh, Assam, and Tamil Nadu. According to the CEO: "Some of this is going live in the next few months, like the concentrates plant in Madhya Pradesh and the Northeast plant in Assam." Regarding the southern expansion, leadership noted: "The land purchase, which we have just done recently in Tamil Nadu, will allow us to open a massive footprint in the South for our snacks business." India ranks among PepsiCo's top 13 global markets. The company posted a profit after tax of ₹905 crore for the 12 months ended December 2025 on total revenue of ₹9,789 crore. ... It only notes that beverage segment competition "went up quite a bit" in 2025, while foods remained the stronger performer with approximately 11% growth.

topic.title: Second 47 Disclosure
topic.claim: Every 'get ready with me' reel buries the paid partnership tag around the 47th second, right after the hook and the outfit reveal.
topic.behaviour: Creators flash 'ad' in small text after they've already got you watching, just before the link in bio.
topic.mechanism: The disclosure exists to satisfy the platform's rule, not to actually tell you upfront what you're watching.
topic.why_now: this pattern has basically become the default across creator ads

violations: The '47th second' is stated as a literal, specific, universal fact ('Every single... reel', 'in the same exact spot', 'Somewhere around the 47th second') and repeated three times (slides 1, 3, 6) as if it were measured data.
